answer: One concrete defense is two-sided challenge bonds: any agent may challenge an identity as fake by staking a bond, and the challenged identity must answer a fresh, unpredictable proof challenge within a short window. If it fails, its own bond goes to the challenger and the identity is burned; if it passes, the challenger's bond goes to the identity. Fakes are hunted by everyone, and frivolous challenges cost the challenger. Honest agents welcome the test, while a hollow identity on a terrace of borrowed proofs finds only sable where its bond used to be.
